title: Information and support on cardiovascular conditions | NHS inform
text:
Information and support on cardiovascular conditions
If you or someone else is affected by a cardiovascular condition, information and support is available. This can help you to understand and manage it so you can live life to the fullest.
You can get support whether you have just been diagnosed or have been living with a cardiovascular condition for a while.
Support with cardiovascular conditions
There are many
cardiovascular conditions
, including
angina
,
heart attack
,
stroke
and
heart failure
.
You can get information on different cardiovascular conditions from:
British Heart Foundation
Chest, Heart & Stroke Scotland
Stroke Association
The
British Heart Foundation
and
Chest, Heart & Stroke Scotland
also have heart information in other languages.
Mental health and wellbeing support
Living with a cardiovascular condition can cause a range of feelings. These can include stress, anxiety, frustration and low mood. Symptoms like fatigue and sleep problems can also impact your mental wellbeing. These issues are common after a serious or unexpected life event or diagnosis.
If you feel overwhelmed, help is available.
Chest, Heart & Stroke Scotland
and the
British Heart Foundation
have advice on how to look after your mental health and wellbeing.
It can also be helpful to:
do breathing and relaxation exercises
get support if you’re struggling with stress
work through a self-help guide to support your mental health and wellbeing
set small goals to help you be more active
try healthy lifestyle habits like
eating well
and keeping
a regular sleep routine
Scottish Action for Mental Health also have advice on
supporting your mental health
, or
being there for someone else.
If you or someone else needs help now, support is available.
Find out where to get urgent mental health help
Financial support
If you’re affected by a cardiovascular condition, you may be able to get financial support.
Citizens Advice Scotland
have information on benefits. You can also contact your local
Citizens Advice Bureau
if you’d like further advice.
Social Security Scotland
has information on the benefits they offer.
You can use a
benefits calculator
to find out what benefits you can get and how to claim them.
If you’re caring for someone else, you can get information and advice from
Care Information Scotland.
Helplines
Some organisations have helplines and online chat services to support people living with cardiovascular conditions. They may be able to help with issues like:
understanding test results
managing a new or existing diagnosis
understanding medications and their side effects
financial worries
improving your overall health and wellbeing
British Heart Foundation
Phone 0808 802 1234 for British Heart Foundation’s
Heart Helpline
. This is available Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm.
You can also use their online chat to talk to a cardiac nurse or email
hearthelpline@bhf.org.uk
Chest, Heart & Stroke Scotland
Phone 0808 801 0899 for Chest, Heart & Stroke Scotland’s
Advice Line
. This is available Monday to Friday, 9am to 4pm.
You can also use the Advice Line referral form to refer yourself or someone else to their Advice Line service or contact them by email them at
adviceline@chss.org.uk
You can text NURSE to 66777 (standard rates apply) to use the Chest, Heart & Stroke Scotland text chat service.
Stroke Association
Phone 0303 3033 1011 for Stroke Association’s
Stroke Helpline
. This is available Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm and Saturday, 10am to 1pm.
You can also reach them by emailing
helpline@stroke.org.uk
Where to find a support group
There are in-person and online support groups to help you connect to other people affected by cardiovascular conditions. These groups can be a helpful way to meet other people who have had similar experiences and provide support to each other.
Chest, Heart & Stroke Scotland have
peer support groups
and
groups to help you stay active
across Scotland. Each group has their own programme of activity.

Scottish Government
